1. The order impugned vide this revision petition is dated 22.03.2022 vide which application under Section 156 (3) Cr.P.C filed by complainant / petitioner for registration of FIR under Sections 420/406/506 r/w Section 120B IPC has been dismissed.

2. The factual matrix of the case are that on 09.06.2020, petitioner entered into an Agreement to Sell with respondent no.2 Warees Ahmed, with respect to property admeasuring 138 Sq. Yds.
bearing Khasra No.222, Plot R129, Jogabai Extension, New Delhi (hereinafter referred to as the "suit property"), for a total sale consideration of Rs.1,65,60,000/-.

Besides this, another Agreement to Sell was entered into between the petitioner and respondent no.2 with respect to 200 Sq. Yds. of suit property for a total sale Syed Ehsan Ahmad Ajmeri Vs. State of NCT of Delhi & Ors.
consideration of Rs.1,74,00,000/-.

entities.text: Syed Ehsan Ahmad Ajmeri Vs. State of NCT of Delhi & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent no.2 paid a sum of Rs.40 Lakhs to the complainant at the time of execution of above agreements.
It was agreed that balance amount will be paid in four installments.

Thereafter, since respondent no.2 had promised to make the balance payment,
petitioner allowed him and his associates to initiate construction work upon the suit property.

However, despite repeated requests and reminder, respondent no.2, in furtherance of malicious intention to cheat and defraud the petitioner and to usurp his property, neither made any further payment nor halted the construction work over the suit property.
Whenever petitioner demanded his balance money or asked the respondents to stop the construction work, he was threatened by them that his son will be implicated in a false criminal case.
Petitioner made various complaints to the police in this regard but police did not take any action.
Thereafter, he filed a Civil Writ Petition bearing No.9193/2020 before Hon'ble High Court seeking directions to the police and SDMC to stop the construction work immediately.

3. On 24.01.2021, respondent no.2 and 3 induced the petitioner to visit the house of respondent no.7 to sign and execute two General Power of Attorneys (GPAs) concerning the suit property and another property of 138 Sq. Yds. near Masjid A1 Noor, with a false promise to pay Rupees One Crore Ninety Lakhs (Rs.1.90 Crores) to him.

However, after signing and execution of GPAs in their favour,
respondents handed over Rs.47 Lakhs to respondent no.8 Advocate Syed Ehsan Ahmad Ajmeri Vs.
State of NCT of Delhi & Ors.

But till date not even a single penny has been paid to petitioner by any of the respondents.

Respondent no.7 Syed Rafi Ahmad retained the original documents and assured the petitioner that he will get the full amount of Rs.1.90 Crores immediately and till then he shall retain the documents and on this pretext, documents were never handed over to him.

Since no payment was made to him, he issued a letter dated 24.08.2021 to the respondents thereby cancelling the GPAs, which was duly replied to by respondents no.2 and 3 claiming that they have paid the amount.

Respondents did not make any payment as promised to the petitioner despite execution of fresh GPAs which has caused him a loss to the tune of Rs.3 Crores and when the petitioner confronted them for their non compliance with the agreement, they threatened him with dire consequences and criminally intimidated him.
Despite making repeated complaints to the local police, ACP and DCP, no action was taken against the respondents.

Hence, the petitioner filed a complaint under Section 200 Cr.PC alongwith an application under Section 156(3) Cr.PC for registration of FIR against the respondents and to investigate the matter in accordance with law.
4. Learned Metropolitan Magistrate vide the impugned order dated 22.03.2022 dismissed the application under Section 156(3) Cr.PC moved by the petitioner and fixed the case for pre-summoning evidence.
Aggrieved by the said order, the petitioner has filed the present revision petition.

sentences.text: I have heard learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the counsels representing respondents no.2 to 8.
I have also perused the trial court record.
6. The various grounds are taken by the petitioner assailing the impugned order.
It is mentioned that the impugned order was passed by the learned Trial Court in a mechanical manner and is without application of mind and same is devoid of reasoning.

Learned Trial Court has failed to appreciate that during pendency of the complaint, the petitioner has learnt that respondents alongwith other accomplices have succeeded in getting electricity meter installed by placing forged and fabricated property documents.
Learned Trial Court has completely brushed aside the documents and allegations made against the respondents.

Learned Trial Court did not appreciate at all the allegations against the respondents with respect to cognizance of offence and as per the observations made by the Apex Court in Lalita Kumari Vs. Govt. of U.P. & Ors., IV (2013) DLT (Crl.)
910 (SC) and Ramesh Kumari Vs. State, II (2006) SLT 387, when a cognizable offence is reported,
the police is required to register the FIR.

sentences.text: It has been stated that registration of FIR is mandatory but despite specific allegations, the police has failed to register the FIR and even the learned Trial Court has not considered this aspect.

9. In Lalita Kumari Vs. Govt. of U.P. & Ors. (supra), in Para 111, the court has observed that registration of FIR is mandatory under Section 154 of the Code, if the information discloses commission of a cognizable offence and no preliminary inquiry is permissible in such a situation.

The Agreement to Sell with him was executed by respondent no.2 on 09.06.2020 and thereafter, on 24.01.2021, respondents no.2 and 3 have induced him to Syed Ehsan Ahmad Ajmeri Vs. State of NCT of Delhi & Ors.

sentences.text: 11. As per the Trial Court record, the petitioner has filed copies of the complaint having due receiving made by PHQ, DCP (SE).
These complaints are dated 14.06.2021 to PHQ and dated 01.11.2021 to the office of DCP (SE) and dated 03.11.2021 to the office of ACP.
The other copies of the complaints filed by the petitioner on record are not bearing any receiving by any of the police authority.
This shows that there is delay of more than 3 months in making the complaint to the police.
As per the ATR on the Trial Court Record filed by SI Manish Tyagi PS Jamia Nagar, the petitioner had filed the petition i.e. WP (C) No.9183 (sic)/ 2020 before the Hon'ble High Court.

Though, the property involved in this Writ Petition is different from the property involved in this petition but the petitioner had given a handwritten undertaking to the respondents, at the time of hearing that he had settled all the disputes with respondent no.2 and now he does not want to pursue his complaint given at SDMC and petition filed before the Hon'ble High Court.

On 27.01.2021, petitioner had visited SDMC office and had given an affidavit that dispute with respondent no.2 in connection with property bearing No.R-212A has been resolved and he has no grievance left against respondent no.2.

Thereafter, petitioner again filed a petition before the Hon'ble High Court vide CONT.CAS(C) No.462/2021 wherein it is alleged that order dated 20.11.2020 of the Hon'ble High Court is not complied with and said petition Syed Ehsan Ahmad Ajmeri Vs. State of NCT of Delhi & Ors.
was also disposed of with the observations that no order is required in this matter.

sentences.text: In Subhkaran Luharuka Vs. State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi), (2010) 170 DLT 516, Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that "... in those cases where the allegations are not very serious and the complainant himself is in possession of evidence to prove his allegations there should be no need to pass orders under Section 156(3) of the Code.

entities.text: Subhkaran Luharuka Vs. State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi), (2010) 170 DLT 516
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The discretion ought to be exercised after proper application of mind and only in those cases where the Magistrate is of the view that the nature of the allegation is such that the complainant himself may not be in a position to collect and produce evidence before the Court and interest of justice demand that the police should step in to help the complainant."

Another landmark judgment touching the facts of this case is of M/S. Skipper Beverages Pvt. Ltd. vs State, 2001 IV AD Delhi 625 wherein the court has observed that the power of directing the police to register a case and initiate investigation under section 156(3) Cr. PC should be exercised judiciously and not in a mechanical manner.

entities.text: M/S. Skipper Beverages Pvt. Ltd. vs State, 2001 IV AD Delhi 625
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When field investigation by the police is not required and complainant is in a position to collect and produce evidence in the court, order for registration of FIR need not be passed.

The entire case of the petitioner is based upon his oral testimony and various documents i.e. Agreement to Sell and GPAs stated to have been executed between him and respondent no.2.

Thereby, learned Trial Court has rightly observed that investigation by the police is not required to dug out the truth and accordingly, the application under Section 156(3) Cr.PC of the petitioner was dismissed.
14.
In view of the aforesaid reasons, there is no illegality and infirmity in the impugned order.
Hence, the revision petition is dismissed.
15. A copy of this order alongwith Trial Court Record be sent back to the learned Trial Court.
16. Revision file be consigned to Record Room.
